newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks end higher, ITC races ahead.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks end higher, ITC races ahead.

text.p: Indian blue chips sprang higher on Monday led by a nearly ten percent jump in index-linked stock ITC, traders said.

The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark 30-share index rallied for a third day running, with the momentum kept intact by foreign buying and technically induced demand for ITC. Dealers said there was no fresh news or speculation motivating the move into the tobacco giant.
ITC shares leapt 42.0 rupees, or nearly ten percent, to end at 478.50 in heavy volumes of 5.20 million shares at the BSE.
"The market is very short on ITC. Some speculators have realised that and are squeezing the shorts," said a trader at a foreign brokerage in Bombay.
Traders said some speculators had to cover their short positions after leading foreign funds turned buyers in the stock last week. They said the fund buying continued in this session.
"It was a double whammy -- foreign institutional buying and short covering in expectation of an auction on the National Stock Exchange this week," one dealer said.
ITC shares attracted a backwardation charge -- indicating a short position -- in the BSE carry forward account ended May 31.
"It was the third consecutive backwardation," the trader at the foreign brokerage said. "Along with ITC, everything is following suit."
"Today's rally in stock prices was a technical correction since most of the stocks had been oversold," said Harish Malhotra of brokerage Malhotra Financial Consultants.
Funds were also buyers in leading soaps and detergents maker Hindustan Lever, tea firm Tata Tea and scooter and motorcycle maker Bajaj Auto.
A likely domestic oil prices hike overhung the market --the government's steering committee is expected to act on June 8.
